<Rep. Maxine Waters, Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, Rep. Al Green, Rep. Brad Sherman, Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, Rep. Bill Foster, Rep. Juan Vargas, Rep. Ayanna Pressley, Rep. Nikema Williams, Rep. Joyce Beatty, Rep. Sean Casten, Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia>: H.R. 3633, the crypto market structure bill Democrats call the ``CALAMITY Act,'' would legitimize the numerous crypto scams of President Trump and his family. The bill also creates new loopholes of other crypto companies not owned by the President to avoid investor protections and national security guardrails. Notably, this legislation impedes, blocks or restricts oversight, funding, and resources to enforce provisions related to national security, conflict of interests, and fraud. The CALAMITY Act would also threaten overall financial stability, as exemptions in the bill are broad enough to create loopholes for participants to migrate from our securities markets to this new crypto one.
Throughout the 2024 campaign trail, President Trump promised to make America the ``crypto capital of the planet and the Bitcoin superpower of the world.''\1\ What he didn't mention was that he and his family were also planning to create several new crypto companies and offer crypto products directly to the public, including foreign governments. For example, in the days before his inauguration and during his Presidency, the President and his family launched a decentralized finance
(defi) platform,\2\ memecoins,\3\ a stablecoin,\4\ a Bitcoin mining company,\5\ a Bitcoin treasury,\6\ Bitcoin ETF,\7\ and more.\8\ Purchases of Trump's crypto products have also enabled access to the President, and have been used by foreign governments to facilitate commercial deals, all generating Trump and his family more than a billion dollars. Separately, Trump has asserted unprecedented control over what were formerly understood to be independent financial regulators, by firing Commissioners and Directors, and asserting approval over the rulewriting process. And notably, President Trump has directed Republicans in Congress\9\ to pass stablecoin and crypto market structure legislation before August recess, even as he and his family roll out new crypto products.\10\
\1\Trump pledges national Bitcoin stockpile, to make US `crypto capital of the planet', USA Today (July 28, 2024); Trump calls for US to be `crypto capital of the planet' in appeal to Nashville bitcoin conference, AP News (July 27, 2024).
\2\Trump Made $57.4 Million From World Liberty Financial, New Filing Discloses, Forbes (June 14, 2025); Trump Rolls Out His New Cryptocurrency Business, New York Times (Sept. 16, 2024).
\3\Donald and Melania Trump launch a pair of meme coins ahead of inauguration, raising serious ethics concerns, CNN (Jan. 20, 2025); Trump faces crypto world backlash after launch of meme coin, The Hill (Jan. 20, 2025).
\4\Trump's Crypto Venture Introduces New Digital Currency, New York Times (Mar. 25, 2025).
\5\Trump family's bitcoin mining venture to go public--as Trump crypto interests grow, CBS News (May 12, 2025).
\6\Trump Media's Bitcoin treasury registration `declared effective' by SEC, CoinTelegraph (June 14, 2025).
\7\Trump Media seeks to launch `Truth Social bitcoin ETF', Financial Times (June 5, 2025).
\8\Trump reports more than $600 million in income from crypto, golf, licensing fees, Reuters (June 14, 2025).
\9\President Trump's AI and Crypto Czar, David Sacks, as well House-Senate Bicameral Working Group on Digital Assets announced the target goal of having stablecoin and market structure legislation through the Senate within the first 100 days of the new Administration. See President Trump's Crypto Czar Outlines Federal Government's New Approach to Digital Assets, wiley (Feb. 5, 2025); Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, Scott: Congress, Trump Administration Committed to Securing U.S. Leadership in Digital Assets (Feb. 4, 2025).
\10\Trump holds long-awaited crypto summit, calls for bill `on his desk' before August, Fortune (Mar. 7, 2025).
It is in this context that on May 5, 2025, Chair Hill released a revised version of crypto market structure legislation, H.R. 3633. In his testimony before the House Financial Services Committee, Timothy Massad, a former Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman and current Research Fellow and Director of the Digital Assets Policy Project at Harvard University, summarized major challenges facing the bill:
With over 200 pages of detailed, complicated
provisions, the implications of which are difficult to
assess, I fear the Clarity Act is likely to have two
principal effects: first, it will guarantee its own
obsolescence, because the technology will evolve and
the particulars of provisions will become outdated or
not relevant. Second, and of far greater danger . . .
it will generate massive exploitation of its provisions
and regulatory arbitrage.\11\
\11\House Committee on Financial Services, Testimony of Timothy G. Massad, Democratic Minority Day: Continuation of American Innovation and the Future of Digital Assets: From Blueprint to a Functional Framework, 119th Cong. (June 6, 2025).
The loopholes in this bill coupled with a self-profiteering President, captured agencies, and non-existent enforcement of current law under the Trump Administration, would allow fraud to proliferate and result in devastating losses for not just crypto consumers, but also for non-crypto investors who are trying to save for college, home ownership, retirement, or other milestones. Passing this bill into law would make Congress complicit in Trump's numerous crypto scams and cause lasting harm to the American economy and public.
PRESIDENT TRUMP'S CRYPTO CONFLICTS OF INTEREST
The CALAMITY Act would not just enable large-scale conflicts of interest from Trump and his family, it would send a message that Congress approves and validates the way he is selling access to the White House, both domestically and abroad. Existing executive branch ethics requirements contain loopholes and gaps that can be easily exploited, and certain conflicts of interest laws exempt the President and Vice President. This has paved the way for unprecedented corruption and unchecked self-profiteering. For example, according to ethics and anti-corruption experts, Democracy Defenders Action:
If President Trump were subject to the same criminal
conflict of interest statute, 18 U.S.C. 208, that
applies to other executive branch employees, he would
have been prohibited from signing the March 23
Executive Order . . . [And] if he were subject to
section 208 like other executive branch employee who
may have interests in stablecoins, he would be barred
from working on legislation that would be viewed as a
particular matter . . .\12\
\12\Democracy Defenders Fund, Trump's Crypto Conflicts of Interest: A Growing Concern (Apr. 23, 2025).
The Trump family's high-profile conflicts of interest were elevated a few days before the presidential inauguration. President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump launched their own memecoins ($TRUMP and $MELANIA), with $TRUMP earning a staggering $350 million in the three weeks after it was launched, from sales and fees alone.\13\ While early, likely inside investors profited off of the memecoins, most investors lost a staggering $2 billion as the coins value plummeted.\14\ Later on, Trump announced that the 220 largest holders would be invited to an exclusive memecoin dinner at his luxury golf resort on May 22nd, for which attendees, including foreign investors, spent millions of dollars to secure a seat.\15\ The CALAMITY Act exempts memecoins from regulation, leaving them, including Trump's memecoin, to operate with no oversight at all. One Committee hearing witness, Professor Timothy Massad, raised a critical point during his testimony:
\13\Helen Partz, Donald Trump's memecoin generated $350M for creators: Report, CoinTelegraph (Mar. 07, 2025).
\14\Early Crypto Traders Had Speedy Profit on Trump Coin as Others Suffered Losses, New York Times (Feb. 9, 2025).
\15\Democracy Defenders Fund, Trump's Crypto Conflicts of Interest: A Growing Concern (Apr. 23, 2025).
In the words of Vitalik Buterin, [memecoins] are
vehicles for `unlimited political bribery,' because
those seeking to curry favor with the Administration--
whether they be individuals, companies or countries--
may purchase the coins, knowing the President will
profit from their actions, while they can still deny
that seeking government favoritism was their purpose.
Instead, they can claim they were merely speculating on
a digital asset.\16\
\16\House Committee on Financial Services, Testimony of Timothy G. Massad, Democratic Minority Day: Continuation of American Innovation and the Future of Digital Assets: From Blueprint to a Functional Framework, 119th Cong. (June 6, 2025).
In addition to dropping or pausing ongoing enforcement cases against Trump's donors and crypto investors,\17\ the SEC has also issued statements declaring that certain digital assets, which include crypto products issued or backed by the Trump family, are not subject to SEC oversight.\18\ More recently, on June 13, the SEC approved the Trump Media and Technology Group's (Trump Media) $2.3 billion Bitcoin treasury deal, one of the largest Bitcoin treasury deals for a public company.\19\ On Monday, June 16, President Trump's social media company, Truth Social, also filed a registration form with the SEC to launch a dual exchange-traded fund (ETF) for Bitcoin and Ether.\20\
\17\Matthew Goldstein, S.E.C. Drops Lawsuit Against Binance, a Crypto Exchange, New York Times (May 29, 2025); Rebecca Balhaus, et. al., Trump Family Has Held Deal Talks With Binance Following Crypto Exchange's Guilty Plea, Wall Street Journal (Mar. 13, 2025).
\18\Crypto group Tron to go public after US pauses probe into billionaire founder, Financial Times (June 16, 2025); Securities and Exchange Commission, Statement on Stablecoins (Apr. 4, 2025); Securities and Exchange Commission, Statement on certain proof-of-work mining activities (Mar. 20, 2025); Securities and Exchange Commission, Staff Statement on Meme Coins (Feb. 27, 2025).
\19\Trump Media's Bitcoin treasury registration `declared effective' by SEC, CoinTelegraph (June 14, 2025).
\20\Trump's Truth Social files S-1 for dual Bitcoin and Ether ETF, CoinTelegraph (June 16, 2025).
Not only is Trump and his family, personally and financially involved in the crypto space through their numerous crypto businesses, the President also stands to be the largest direct competitor in the ecosystem. In addition to flouting ethics standards, Trump has continued to undermine the independence of the historically bipartisan independent federal financial agencies. Trump has targeted Democratic appointees who are protected from removal by the president and can only be terminated for cause and fired the Democratic Directors of the National Credit Union Administration, and Commissioners of the Federal Trade Commission. In her testimony before the House Financial Services Committee, Amanda Fischer, Policy Director and COO at Better Markets, discussed this issue:
Federal financial regulatory agencies are under siege
in the current Administration. Democratic
commissioners, dually nominated by the President and
confirmed by the Senate, have been fired without cause,
with the Supreme Court in a two-page decision declining
to place an injunction on the firings. [Soon], the CFTC
will only have one Commissioner, with no further
Commissioner nominations on the horizon. Absent a
nomination by the President, the SEC is separately set
to have a three-member Republican-only commission by
the end of 2025, despite the statutory requirement and
long history of being bipartisan.\21\
\21\House Committee on Financial Services, Testimony of Amanda Fischer, Democratic Minority Day: Continuation of American Innovation and the Future of Digital Assets: From Blueprint to a Functional Framework, 119th Cong. (June 6, 2025).
This represents an attack on critical democratic safeguards and sends a message to both Democratic and Republican leaders at two regulators overseeing this market, the SEC and CFTC.
